title: The Life Is In The Blood

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But you must not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground like water. You must not eat in your own towns the tithe of your grain and new wine and olive oil, or the firstborn of your herds and flocks, or whatever you have vowed to give, or your freewill offerings or special gifts. Instead, you are to eat them in the presence of the Lord your God at the place the Lord your God will choose—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levites from your towns—and you are to rejoice before the Lord your God in everything you put your hands to. - Deut 12:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Woven through these worship instructions is a solemn command: "you must not eat the blood." Throughout the law, blood was treated as sacred because "the life of a creature is in the blood" (Lev 17:11). Blood represented life itself, and life belongs to God. So the blood was to be poured out, treated with reverence, never casually consumed. This was not an arbitrary rule but a profound teaching about the sacredness of life and the seriousness of atonement.

Behind this command lay a deep truth that would echo through all of Scripture: life is costly, and the forgiveness of sin requires the shedding of blood. Every sacrifice in Israel's worship, with its poured-out blood, was teaching the people that sin is serious and that atonement comes at the cost of life. The blood pointed to a price being paid.

All of this finds its fulfillment in Jesus. The blood of countless animals could never truly take away sin — it only pointed forward to the one whose blood would. "Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness" (Heb 9:22), and Jesus shed His own precious blood to accomplish what all those sacrifices could not. His blood, poured out on the cross, is the true and final atonement for our sin. When we come to the Lord's Supper and take the cup, we remember that His blood was shed for us. The reverence for blood in the old law prepared God's people to grasp the immeasurable worth of Christ's blood. Give thanks today for the life He poured out to give you life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I grasp how seriously God treats sin and the cost of atonement?
- What does it mean to me that Jesus shed His own blood for my forgiveness?
- How does this deepen my gratitude at the Lord's Supper?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You poured out Your own precious blood to accomplish what no sacrifice could — the forgiveness of my sin. I could never earn such a gift. Thank You for the life You gave to give me life. Help me never take Your sacrifice for granted. Amen.
